title: Count Stepping Numbers in Range
summary: Determine the count of stepping numbers within the range from the string representation of a lower bound to an upper bound, inclusive.
statement: Determine the count of stepping numbers within the range from the string representation of a lower bound to an upper bound, inclusive. A stepping number is defined as an integer where the absolute difference between any two consecutive digits is exactly one. The result should be given modulo 10^9 + 7, and stepping numbers must not have leading zeros.
constraints: A positive integer is stepping when every adjacent decimal digit differs by exactly one.
Count stepping numbers in the inclusive range low through high.
hints: Count valid numbers no greater than one bound with digit DP.
State stores digit position, previous chosen digit, whether a nonleading digit has started, and tightness.
Allow a new significant digit only when its distance from the previous digit is one; subtract count(low-1) from count(high).
Every bounded representation follows one DP path, and the transition enforces the stepping condition at each adjacent significant digit.
editorial: Every bounded representation follows one DP path, and the transition enforces the stepping condition at each adjacent significant digit.

tests.explanation: The values one through nine plus ten are stepping, giving ten.
Only 98 and 101 qualify in this range.
